summary: Senkyo Sakawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology who studied at Rissho University until 1965. He was an associate professor at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 1981) and later professor at Rissho University.

Senmyo Naniwa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University, studying under Genjun Sasaki, Mohan G. Dhadphale, J. R. Joshi, and P. V. Bapat. In 2005, he held posts at Bukkyo University and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Sensho Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1962 to 1971 and served there as a professor from circa 1985 to 2008.

Sensho Murakami (1851–1929) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani University, Toyo University, and under Ryomon, Yukitada Takeda, and Gokan Un'ei. He served as a lecturer and professor at the University of Tokyo (1888, 1917–1923).

Seok-hyeong Kim is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University from circa 1928 to 1932. He later served as a professor at Dongguk University and as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University.

Seong-Uk Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He holds a post as Cho Associate Professor in Korean Culture and Religion at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Seongjoon Cheong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD from Dongguk University (1995–1999). He was a research fellow at the Translation Institute of Tibetan Buddhist Canon (2015–2016) and a research professor at Uiduk University (2023–2024).

Seraphim Rose (1934–1982) was a figure in religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Alan Watts and attended CIIS, USC, and UC Berkeley (circa 1957–1961), later holding a post in the Russian Orthodox Patriarchal Parishes in the United States.

Sergej Konstantinovich Bulich (1859–1921) specialized in linguistics and Indology. After studying at Kazan State University, Berlin, Jena, and Leipzig under scholars including Baudouin de Courtenay, he became an extraordinary professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Saint Petersburg State University in 1891.

Sergey Burmistrov is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who received his D. Sci. from Saint Petersburg State University (2007–2010). He taught at Saint Petersburg State University and became a leading researcher at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts in 2011.

Sergey Malov (1880–1957) worked in linguistics, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kazan Theological Academy and Saint Petersburg State University, he directed several Kazan institutes (1917–1922) and headed the Sector of Turkic Languages at the Institute of Linguistics (1934–1957).

Sergey Oldenburg (1863–1934) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev. He became a professor there in 1894, perpetual secretary of the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences, and director of the Asiatic Museum.

Sergiu Anatol Al-George (1922–1981) was a Romanian scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. A pupil of Mircea Eliade, he studied at the University of Bucharest and the University of Delhi, and taught at the University of Bucharest from 1971 to 1973.

Serinity Young (1944–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1990 under Alex Wayman and Vidya Dehejia, later holding posts at Southern Methodist University and the American Museum of Natural History.
Sesso Oda (1901–1966) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded Zuigan Goto (circa 1928–1965). His students included Soko Morinaga and Gary Snyder.

Seth Segall is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from Southern Illinois University Carbondale (1975–1977). He served as an assistant clinical professor at Yale School of Medicine (1981–2017) and lecturer at Purchase College (2012–2017).
Seton Uhlhorn is an Indology scholar who studied as a PhD candidate in South Asian studies and served as an instructional fellow in Hindi-Urdu at Harvard University (attested 2020, 2026).

Seung-yeon Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and archaeology who completed doctoral studies under Lee Sang-hae. Lee has held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties.

Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Seoul National University and a PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Koh worked at Geumgang University (2017–2025) and became an associate professor at Seoul National University in 2025.

Seungsahn Haengwon (1927–2004) was a Buddhist master who studied at Dongguk University and under teachers including Kobong Sunim, whom he succeeded in 1957. In 1970, he founded the Kwan Um School of Zen.
